title: Cold Calling & Inquiry Handling Masterclass
titleCn: 冷电话与询盘处理实战课
desc: Emma和James用真实对话拆解冷电话30秒开场公式、绕过前台技巧、异议处理方法，以及询盘分类、回复模板和跟进节奏，新人必听。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Welcome back to TradeTalk! I'm Emma, and today we're tackling the two scariest things for new trade professionals: cold calling and inquiry handling.
lines.cn: 欢迎回到TradeTalk！我是Emma，今天我们要聊外贸新人最害怕的两件事：冷电话和询盘处理。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Great topic, Emma. I still remember my first cold call — I was so nervous I forgot my own company name. But once you have a system, it becomes much easier.
lines.cn: 好话题，Emma。我还记得我的第一次冷电话——我紧张到忘了自己公司的名字。但一旦你有了系统，就会容易很多。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Exactly! So let's start with cold calling. James, what's the golden rule for the first 30 seconds?
lines.cn: 没错！我们先从冷电话开始。James，前30秒的黄金法则是什么？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: The 30-second formula is simple: who you are, what value you bring, and what you want. For example: 'Hi, this is James from Wenzhou New Era Stationery. We help UK retailers increase their marker category margin by 15% with eco-friendly refillable products. Would you be open to a quick 10-minute call next week?' That's it — no fluff, no small talk.
lines.cn: 30秒公式很简单：你是谁，你能带来什么价值，你想要什么。比如：'嗨，我是温州新时代文具的James。我们用环保可换芯产品帮助英国零售商提升15%的马克笔品类利润率。您下周有空通个10分钟的电话吗？'就这样——没有废话，没有寒暄。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Love that. But what about the gatekeeper? You know, the receptionist who says 'can I ask what this is regarding?'
lines.cn: 很喜欢。但是前台怎么办？你知道的，那种说'请问您有什么事吗'的接待员？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Ah, the gatekeeper. The key is to be confident and brief. Don't sound like a salesperson. Say something like: 'I'm calling about our eco-friendly marker range that several UK retailers are already using. Could you put me through to the purchasing manager?' If they push back, offer to send an email first — but always ask for the transfer first.
lines.cn: 啊，前台。关键是自信和简短。不要听起来像销售员。说类似这样的话：'我打电话是关于我们的环保马克笔系列，已经有几家英国零售商在用了。请帮我转接采购经理好吗？'如果他们拒绝，主动提出先发邮件——但一定要先请求转接。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Great advice. Now, what's the most common objection you hear on cold calls?
lines.cn: 好建议。那么，冷电话中最常见的异议是什么？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: The most common one is 'I'm busy, just send me an email.' Most new sellers give up at this point. But here's the trick: agree with them, then ask for one specific thing. Say: 'I completely understand — I'll send a short email with our catalog. Would it be OK if I follow up with you next Tuesday to see if you had any questions?' This way, you get a specific follow-up time instead of just disappearing into their inbox.
lines.cn: 最常见的是'我很忙，发邮件给我吧'。大多数新卖家在这时候就放弃了。但技巧是：同意他们，然后要求一个具体的东西。说：'我完全理解——我会发一封简短的邮件附我们的目录。我下周二跟进您，看看您有没有问题，可以吗？'这样，你得到了一个具体的跟进时间，而不是消失在他们的收件箱里。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: That's brilliant. Now let's switch to inquiry handling. When a buyer sends an inquiry that just says 'send me your best price', what should you do?
lines.cn: 太棒了。现在我们切换到询盘处理。当买家发询盘只说'给我你们的最优价格'时，你该怎么做？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Don't just send a price! That's the biggest mistake. You need to qualify the inquiry first. Reply with something like: 'Thank you for your interest! To give you the most accurate price, could you confirm: 1) Which product category? 2) What quantity? 3) Any custom requirements? I'll send a detailed quote within 24 hours.' This does two things: it shows you're professional, and it filters out the tire-kickers who aren't serious.
lines.cn: 不要只发价格！这是最大的错误。你需要先筛选询盘。回复类似这样的话：'感谢您的兴趣！为了给您最准确的价格，您能确认吗：1）哪个产品类别？2）多少数量？3）有定制需求吗？我会在24小时内发送详细报价。'这样做有两个好处：显示你很专业，同时筛选掉不认真的闲逛客。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Right. And how do you classify inquiries? I've heard about A, B, C classification.
lines.cn: 对。你怎么分类询盘？我听说过A、B、C分类法。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Exactly. A-class inquiries are specific: they know the product, quantity, and requirements. These are hot leads — reply within 2 hours. B-class inquiries have some detail but are vague — they might be comparing suppliers. Reply within 24 hours and ask clarifying questions. C-class inquiries are just 'send catalog' or 'best price' with no details. These are tire-kickers — send a standard reply and move on. Don't waste too much time on C-class.
lines.cn: 没错。A类询盘很具体：他们知道产品、数量和要求。这些是热线索——2小时内回复。B类询盘有一些细节但很模糊——他们可能在比较供应商。24小时内回复，问澄清问题。C类询盘只是'发目录'或'最优价格'，没有任何细节。这些是闲逛客——发标准回复然后继续。不要在C类上浪费太多时间。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: That's a great system. Now, what about follow-up? How many times should you follow up, and how often?
lines.cn: 很好的系统。那么跟进呢？应该跟进多少次，多久一次？

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: The golden follow-up rhythm is: Day 1 — send the initial reply. Day 3 — follow up with something new (a new product, a case study, or a special offer). Day 7 — follow up with industry news or market insights. Day 14 — final follow-up, say 'I don't want to clutter your inbox, but let me know if you're interested.' After that, put them in a long-term nurture list and reach out once a month. The key is: every follow-up must provide new value. Never just say 'just following up' — that's annoying and useless.
lines.cn: 黄金跟进节奏是：第1天——发送初始回复。第3天——用新东西跟进（新产品、案例研究或特别优惠）。第7天——用行业新闻或市场洞察跟进。第14天——最后跟进，说'我不想占用您的收件箱，但如果您感兴趣请告诉我'。之后，把他们放入长期培养列表，每月联系一次。关键是：每次跟进都必须提供新价值。永远不要只说'只是跟进一下'——那很烦人也没用。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Wise words, James. So to summarize: cold calling is about the 30-second value formula, handling gatekeepers with confidence, and turning objections into next steps. Inquiry handling is about qualifying first, classifying A/B/C, and following up with value every time.
lines.cn: 金玉良言，James。总结一下：冷电话的关键是30秒价值公式、自信地应对前台、把异议变成下一步。询盘处理的关键是先筛选、A/B/C分类、每次跟进都提供价值。

lines.speaker: james
lines.en: Exactly! Remember: every call and every email is a chance to build trust. Be professional, be brief, and always provide value. That's how you turn strangers into customers.
lines.cn: 没错！记住：每一通电话和每一封邮件都是建立信任的机会。专业、简短、永远提供价值。这就是你把陌生人变成客户的方法。

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: Perfect. Thanks for sharing your wisdom, James. And thanks to all our listeners — keep practicing, and we'll see you next time on TradeTalk!
lines.cn: 完美。感谢分享你的智慧，James。感谢所有听众——继续练习，我们下期TradeTalk再见！
